station: New York Central Park (Belvedere Castle), GHCN USW00094728
license: NOAA/NWS data are U.S. Government works: public domain, commercial use allowed (17 U.S.C. 105). Open-Meteo free API is non-commercial only, so it is not used.

tmaxF.note: Monthly normal daily maximum, NWS New York (OKX), 1991-2020.

tminF.note: Monthly normal daily minimum, NWS New York (OKX), 1991-2020.

precipDays.note: Days with precipitation >= 0.01 in. Jan, Mar, Aug, Sep, Dec are the 1991-2020 normals printed in NWS monthly climate reports (CLM) for Central Park. Other months are estimates from the NOAA normals table as recalled; run scripts/fetch-climate.mjs to replace them.

snowDays.note: Days with snowfall >= 0.1 in, 1991-2020; table in the article cites NOAA. Secondary source until fetch-climate.mjs reads NCEI directly.

hotDays.note: Average days with high >= 90 F by month, NWS Central Park table (1869-present averages, about 15 a year).

stormDays.note: Days with weather bad enough to empty sidewalks: snowstorms Dec-Mar, nor'easters in spring and fall, thunderstorms in summer. Game design estimate; no single NOAA normal exists.

cloudyShareOfDryDays.note: Share of dry days shown as cloudy. Estimate.

sources.note: Martinez-de-Albeniz and BelKaid: street-front stores lose about 7.4% of traffic on rainy days.
Foursquare with AccuWeather: heavy rain cut restaurant foot traffic by about 10-11% in winter and summer.
Placer.ai: retail visits fell 8.6% nationwide in a storm week, 20-30% in the hardest-hit states.
Fiserv via Nation's Restaurant News: restaurant foot traffic -3.6% in a stormy second half of January.
Foursquare 2016: up to 40% drop in foot traffic during major weather events; 0.7 sits between storm-week and peak-day losses.
No study with a number found; small drop assumed because people stay indoors at midday.
